provenance.row: B4 control 2 of 2 - the second phantom-release direction
provenance.subject: lagging member CONFLICTING at M must produce ONE shared next patch, with both manifests moved EXACTLY once
provenance.design_reference: docs/aben-design.md section 9, B4 control pair, and section 3's mutation controls: 'lagging-member-conflicting-at-M must produce one shared next patch with both manifests moved exactly once'

expected.exactly_once: each manifest moves ONCE. A second pass over the patched tree must emit an empty patch; a member moved twice, or moved to different versions, fails this control even if the final versions look right.
expected.driver: a2a-gateway-image - the member whose conflicting occupancy at M forced the mint. The design requires patches to be labelled with the driving member, so a correct version reached without naming the driver is still a failure of this row.
expected.why: step 4: next-patch of the group maximum applies ONLY when M cannot serve. Here M cannot serve because a2a-gateway-image occupies 1.27.2 with a source identity that is not the intended one - occupied bytes prove a different source, which is the CONFLICTING fork of the partial state, not the recoverable one.

construction.warning: Counterfactual, like its sibling control. The conflicting identity is a DELIBERATELY SYNTHETIC 40-hex string that is not a commit in this repository - it must not resolve, because the point is that it differs from the intended source identity. Do not 'fix' it into a real SHA: a real commit could accidentally match the intended identity and silently convert this control into the recoverable case, which is the one thing it exists to distinguish from.
construction.differs_from_sibling_in_exactly_one_resp: whether ghcr.io/awebai/a2a-gateway occupies 1.27.2 at all, and with what identity. Everything else - both members, M, the aweb-server half, the 1.27.1 anchors - is identical to control-lagging-absent by construction, so the two controls isolate the recoverable/conflicting fork and nothing else.
